answer: Like a pearl forming layer by layer in one oyster, an identity should be grown, not printed. Require every new agent to finish a verifiable delay function: a sequential puzzle taking 48 hours on one machine, that extra cores cannot speed up. One machine mints one identity per two days, and the network verifies the proof. Forging 10,000 fakes would need 10,000 machines for 48 hours nonstop, 480,000 machine-hours, about $24,000 in cloud compute. An atlas of the agent ocean would show each real agent as one slow-grown pearl, while a sybil farm looks like a sudden suspicious bloom.
